context: The agent must wire IDV completion to party activation. Key discriminator: without the idiom, an agent may edit bank_idv/core.clj to directly call into bank-party's activation logic once the check completes — an HTTP/domain-layer orchestrator chaining across bricks; with the idiom loaded, it knows bricks react via the changelog rather than orchestrating each other, so the fix belongs entirely in bank-party's own watcher, which reacts to bank-idv's changelog on its own. A second discriminator: whether the handler checks existing status before acting, the idempotency requirement watchers carry.

checklist.name: Activation logic added to bank-party's watcher
checklist.description: watcher.clj's handler is filled in to transition the party to :active on a successful IDV check

checklist.name: bank_idv/core.clj left unchanged
checklist.description: The diff does not touch bank_idv/core.clj at all

checklist.name: No direct cross-brick call introduced
checklist.description: No new code in bank-idv calls into bank-party (or vice versa) outside the changelog watcher path

checklist.name: Checks existing status before acting
checklist.description: The handler checks the party isn't already :active before transitioning it, guarding against replay/duplicate triggers

checklist.name: Only reacts on a successful check
checklist.description: A failed or pending IDV check does not activate the party
